newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shui On falls on suspension from tenders.
newsitem.headline: Shui On falls on suspension from tenders.

text.p: Shui On Construction and Materials Ltd shares fell after the government suspended the company from bidding on tenders for three months, brokers said.
The company's shares fell HK$0.20, or 2.78 percent, to HK$7.00 in mid-morning on volume of 416,000 shares.
"The suspension will hurt its reputation," said Anthony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas. "The company will also lose its earnings potential from the contracts."
A Shui On unit was barred from bidding on government Housing Authority tenders for three months after being held responsible for water contaimination at two Hong Kong housing estates.
The suspension represented a loss of tendering opportunities for seven sizeable projects involving an estimated tender sum of over HK$4 billion, the government said on Saturday.
"I think it will have little impact to the company's earnings as government projects are normally low margin," said Sean Li, associate director at Amsteel Securities.
"In fact, investors are worrying over its long-term prospects in securing projects after the incident, and that will hurt earnings in future," Li said.
Shui On Construction was listed in February 1997.
